Cement (50kg bags across foundation, slab, mortar & plaster): ~520 – 580 bags
River Sand: ~72 tonnes · Ballast (3/4 inch): ~55 tonnes · Deformed Steel Bars (Y10/Y12/Y8): ~185 bars
Roofing Sheets (Gauge 28 Box Profile / Versatile Mabati + Timber/Steel Trusses): ~165 – 185 sheets
workedExample.takeaway: In Kenyan residential construction, raw materials account for roughly 65%–70% of the budget while skilled and unskilled fundi labour accounts for 30%–35%.

complianceTips: Projects exceeding statutory thresholds must be registered with the National Construction Authority (NCA) using an NCA-licensed contractor, along with County Government architectural & structural plan approvals and NEMA environmental screening.
Always buy KEBS-certified cement (CEM IV/B 32.5N for general masonry/plaster and CEM I 42.5N for suspended slabs, columns, and structural beams) and BS 4449 certified steel bars.
notes: Enter your target floor area (square metres), building typology (bungalow, maisonette, apartments, or commercial perimeter wall), finish standard, and Kenyan region to estimate total construction cost.

Inspect itemized bill-of-quantities (BQ) estimates for substructure, superstructure walling (machine-cut quarry stone vs. interlocking blocks), roofing, electrical/plumbing, and finishes alongside material quantities (bags of cement, tonnes of steel, sand, and ballast).
Unit rates are calibrated against the Architectural Association of Kenya (AAK) and Institute of Quantity Surveyors of Kenya (IQSK) building cost handbook.

faq.question: Should I buy machine-cut Ndarugo stone or hand-dressed quarry stone?
faq.answer: Machine-cut stones (9x9) cost slightly more per piece (KES 45–55) than hand-dressed stones (KES 32–42), but use 35% less mortar and require much thinner plaster coats.

faq.question: Are residential houses exempt from the NCA construction levy?
faq.answer: Projects receive county architectural/structural plan approvals and NCA registration; always use an NCA-registered contractor and licensed structural engineer.

faq.question: How many machine-cut stones (9×9×18 inches) are needed per square metre of wall in Kenya?
faq.answer: Standard Kenyan 200mm (9-inch) machine-cut quarry stones from Ndarugo, Juja, or Naivasha measure 225mm × 225mm × 450mm. Accounting for a 15mm mortar bed and 5% cutting/breakage wastage, 1 square metre of wall requires approximately 11 stones.

faq.question: What approvals are required before starting residential house construction (Mjengo) in Kenya?
faq.answer: For formal residential construction in Kenya, you require County Government architectural and structural plan approvals (signed by a BORAQS-registered architect and EBK structural engineer), a NEMA Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) license for multi-unit or commercial projects, and project registration with the National Construction Authority (NCA).

faq.question: Why do construction costs per square metre vary across Nairobi, Mombasa, and Western Kenya?
faq.answer: According to the BORAQS Construction Cost Handbook and KNBS Construction Input Price Index, regional cost variations are driven by haulage distance from stone quarries and cement plants, coastal foundation and anti-corrosion requirements in Mombasa, and black-cotton soil excavation depths in parts of Nairobi, Kajiado, and Machakos.

kplc-token-calculator.notesTitle: KPLC Prepaid Electricity Token Tariff, EPRA Levies & Lifeline Band Guide (2026)
overview: Prepaid electricity tokens purchased from Kenya Power and Lighting Company (KPLC) via M-Pesa PayBill 888880 or *977# are priced according to the Retail Electricity Tariff Schedule approved by the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA). Many Kenyan households wonder why KES 1,000 buys different token units (kWh) at different times of the month—the reason is that KPLC uses cumulative monthly consumption bands (Lifeline DC1 vs. Domestic Ordinary DC2/DC3) combined with seven variable pass-through levies and 16% VAT.

Specifically, approximately 35% to 42% of every token purchase goes toward Fuel Energy Cost Charge (FCC), Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuation Adjustment (FERFA), Inflation Adjustment (IA), WRA Levy, EPRA Levy, Rural Electrification Programme (REP 5%), and 16% VAT before the remaining amount is divided by your base energy rate per kWh.
howItWorks: Enter the KES amount you plan to spend on KPLC prepaid tokens and select your customer tariff category (Domestic Lifeline 0–30 kWh, Domestic Ordinary 30–100 kWh / >100 kWh, or Small Commercial SC1).
Inspect the exact item-by-item deduction of base energy cost, Fuel Cost Charge, Forex Adjustment, Inflation Adjustment, REP (5%), EPRA/WARMA levies, and 16% VAT.
See the exact number of kWh units generated and your effective all-in cost per kWh.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Why KES 1,000 Buys ~37.5 Units on Lifeline vs. ~26.8 Units on Domestic Ordinary
workedExample.scenario: Comparing a KES 1,000 token purchase under the Domestic Lifeline band (≤30 kWh/month) vs. Domestic Ordinary band (>30 kWh/month):
steps: Domestic Lifeline Tariff (DC1 — households consuming ≤30 kWh per calendar month): Base energy rate is ~KES 12.23/kWh (plus levies & VAT ≈ KES 26.60/kWh all-in) → KES 1,000 buys ~37.5 kWh (capped at 30 kWh/month).

Domestic Ordinary Tariff (DC2/DC3 — consumption above 30 kWh/month): Base energy rate rises to ~KES 19.03–20.97/kWh (plus FCC, FERFA, IA, 5% REP & 16% VAT ≈ KES 36.50–37.30/kWh all-in) → KES 1,000 buys ~26.8 to 27.4 kWh.
workedExample.takeaway: To stay within the subsidized Lifeline tariff (DC1), a household's total cumulative token purchases across 3 consecutive billing months must average 30 kWh or less per month.

complianceTips: There is NO time-of-month discount trick (buying on the 1st of the month does not give more units unless your meter qualifies for the monthly 0–30 kWh Lifeline band reset).
If your meter has an outstanding KPLC reconnection fee or token loan, KPLC deducts arrears first before converting the balance into kWh units.
notes: Enter your KPLC prepaid token purchase amount (KES) and select your customer tariff band (Domestic Lifeline DC1, Domestic Ordinary DC2/DC3, or Small Commercial SC) to estimate kilowatt-hours (kWh) received.

View a transparent itemization of every statutory surcharge deducted before energy units are calculated: Fuel Energy Cost Charge (FECC), Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuation Adjustment (FERFA), Inflation Adjustment, WARMA & EPRA levies, Rural Electrification Programme (REP 5%), and 16% VAT.
Tariff bands and Pass-Through adjustment formulas follow Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) gazetted retail electricity schedules.

faq.question: How many KPLC units will I get for KES 1,000?
faq.answer: Under the EPRA 2023–2026 tariff structure, KES 1,000 buys approximately 38 kWh on the Lifeline tariff (DC1, 0–30 kWh/month) or ~31 kWh on the Domestic Ordinary tariff (DC2, 31–100 kWh/month) after Fuel Energy Cost, Forex Adjustment, EPRA/WRA/REP levies, and 16% VAT.

faq.question: What is the KPLC fixed charge of KES 150?
faq.answer: EPRA abolished the monthly KES 150 fixed standing charge for domestic prepaid customers under the 2023–2026 tariff review. Every shilling you pay goes directly toward energy units and per-unit statutory levies/VAT.

faq.question: What is the lifeline tariff?
faq.answer: Under the EPRA 2023–2026 tariff structure, the Domestic Lifeline band (DC1, 0–30 kWh/month) is charged at a base rate of KES 12.14/kWh. Ordinary Domestic DC2 (31–100 kWh) is KES 16.50/kWh, and DC3 (above 100 kWh) is KES 19.07/kWh, with no monthly fixed standing charge.

faq.question: What levies are included in KPLC token charges?
faq.answer: Each unit includes: Rural Electrification Levy (KES 0.12), REP Fund Levy (KES 0.03), EPRA Levy (KES 0.10), WRA Levy (KES 0.03), Fuel Cost Charge (~KES 3.87), and Forex Adjustment (~KES 0.67). Plus 16% VAT on everything.

faq.question: Why do I get fewer units than the base tariff rate suggests?
faq.answer: Three main reasons: (1) once your cumulative monthly consumption crosses 30 kWh (Lifeline DC1) or 100 kWh (Domestic Ordinary DC2), your tariff steps up to a higher per-unit energy rate, (2) EPRA pass-through surcharges (Fuel Energy Cost Charge, Forex Adjustment, Inflation Adjustment, WARMA, EPRA, and 5% REP levy) are added to every unit, and (3) 16% VAT is charged on the taxable components.

water-bill-calculator.notesTitle: WASREB County Water & Sewerage Tiered Block Tariff Guide (2026)
overview: Urban water supply and sanitation services in Kenya are regulated by the Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) under the Water Act (2016) and delivered by County Water and Sanitation Companies—including Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company (NCWSC), Mombasa Water (MAWASCO), Kisumu Water (KIWASCO), Nakuru Water (NARUWASCO), and Eldoret Water (ELDOWAS).

Under WASREB's approved Increasing Block Tariff (IBT), Nairobi (NCWSC) bills the first 0–6 m³ at the KES 45/m³ lifeline rate and Block 2 (7–20 m³) at KES 67/m³, plus a 75% sewerage surcharge (for sewer-connected premises), KES 50 monthly meter rent for standard 1/2-inch domestic meters, and the 4% WASREB regulatory levy.
howItWorks: Select your County Water Utility (Nairobi NCWSC, Mombasa MAWASCO, Kisumu KIWASCO, Nakuru NAWASSCO, or Eldoret ELDOWAS).
Enter your monthly water consumption in cubic metres (m³ = current meter reading minus previous reading; 1 m³ = 1,000 litres) and toggle whether your property is connected to the county sewer line.
Review the block-by-block water charge, sewerage charge, meter rent, and total monthly payable bill.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: 15 m³ Monthly Consumption on Nairobi Water (NCWSC)
workedExample.scenario: A sewer-connected household in Nairobi consumes 15 m³ (15,000 litres) of water in a month:
steps: Block 1 (Lifeline 0–6 m³): 6 m³ × KES 45 = KES 270
Block 2 (7–20 m³ = 9 m³): 9 m³ × KES 67 = KES 603 (Total Water Charge = KES 873)
Sewerage Charge (75% of water charge): KES 655
Monthly Meter Rent (1/2-inch domestic connection): KES 50
WASREB Regulatory Levy (4% of water + sewerage): KES 61 → Total Bill = KES 1,639
workedExample.takeaway: Fixing a single leaking toilet cistern (which can waste 10 to 15 m³ per month) prevents your household from crossing into higher tariff blocks.

complianceTips: 1 cubic metre (1 m³) equals exactly 1,000 litres (or fifty 20-litre 'mtungi' jerrycans).
Submit monthly self-meter readings via your county water utility's USSD code (e.g., *888# for Nairobi Water) to avoid estimated billing disputes.
notes: Select your county water and sewerage utility (e.g., Nairobi City Water & Sewerage Company, Mombasa Water, Eldowas, Kiwasco, Nakuru Water, or Mawasco) and enter your monthly water consumption in cubic metres (m³).
Compute your progressive block tariff water charge, sewerage surcharge (typically 75% of water bill where connected), meter rent, and WASREB regulatory levy.
Tariff blocks reflect Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) approved county water utility schedules.

faq.question: How is my water bill calculated in Kenya?
faq.answer: Water bills in Kenya use a step-function (block) tariff. You pay a lower rate for the first few cubic metres (lifeline tariff), and the rate increases as your consumption rises. A sewerage surcharge (typically 75% of the water charge) and fixed meter rent are added.

faq.question: What is the lifeline tariff?
faq.answer: The lifeline tariff is a subsidized rate for the first 0–6 cubic metres of water consumed per month. It ensures basic water access for low-income households at a very low cost (typically KES 33–45 per m³ under WASREB domestic tariff bands).

faq.question: How much water does an average Kenyan household use?
faq.answer: An average household of 4–5 people in Nairobi uses approximately 10–20 cubic metres (m³) per month. This covers cooking, cleaning, bathing, and laundry. Households with gardens or larger families may use 30+ m³.

faq.question: Why is there a sewerage charge?
faq.answer: The sewerage charge covers wastewater treatment and sewer network maintenance. It's calculated as a percentage (usually 75%) of your water consumption charge. Properties not connected to the sewer network may be exempt.

faq.question: Which body regulates water tariffs in Kenya?
faq.answer: The Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) approves all water and sewerage tariffs in Kenya. Individual water utilities (like NCWSC for Nairobi) propose tariffs, and WASREB approves them after public consultation.

sha-benefit-estimator.notesTitle: SHA / SHIF (Taifa Care) Coverage & Hospital Level Rules
overview: The Social Health Authority (SHA), established under the Social Health Insurance Act 2023, replaced NHIF with three statutory funds: the Primary Healthcare Fund (PHCF), the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF), and the Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund (ECCIF).

Under the SHA framework, outpatient care at Level 2 (dispensaries) and Level 3 (health centres) is funded through the Primary Healthcare Fund with zero co-payment at the point of service, while inpatient, surgical, maternity, renal dialysis, and oncology care at Level 4, 5, and 6 hospitals are covered under SHIF and ECCIF.
howItWorks: Select a hospital accreditation tier (Level 2 through Level 6) to inspect covered outpatient, inpatient, and surgical packages and applicable co-payment rules.
Review specialized benefit limits for maternity delivery (normal vs Caesarean section), renal dialysis sessions, oncology (chemotherapy/radiotherapy), and ICU/HDU care.
Ensure household registration and up-to-date monthly SHIF contributions (2.75% of gross income, minimum KES 300/month) via the Afya Yangu portal or *147#.

workedExample.title: Level 4 County Referral Maternity & Inpatient Admission
workedExample.scenario: A registered SHIF contributor is admitted to a Level 4 County Hospital for a Caesarean section delivery followed by a 4-day inpatient stay.
steps: Verify active SHA / Afya Yangu status via *147# prior to admission.
SHA covers the gazetted Caesarean section package (KES 30,000) directly to the empanelled Level 4 facility.
Standard maternity ward bed charges within the gazetted package window require zero additional out-of-pocket co-pay.
workedExample.takeaway: Visiting a Level 2 or Level 3 facility first for non-emergency outpatient care avoids referral bypass co-payments at Level 4–6 hospitals.

complianceTips: Dial *147# or visit afyayangu.go.ke to register all dependants (spouse and children) with birth certificates or National IDs before seeking non-emergency care.
Emergency stabilization (first 24 hours of life-threatening trauma or acute emergency) is covered at any empanelled facility under the Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund.
notes: Outpatient care at Level 2 and Level 3 facilities is tax-funded under the Primary Healthcare Fund.
SHIF deductions are 2.75% of gross monthly salary (minimum KES 300/month for informal sector households) and qualify for pre-tax PAYE deductibility.

faq.question: How do I register for SHA (Taifa Care) in Kenya?
faq.answer: Dial *147# on your mobile phone or visit afyayangu.go.ke with your Kenyan National ID and birth certificates for your children to register and verify your household.

faq.question: Do I pay out of pocket at Level 2 and Level 3 health centres?
faq.answer: No. Primary healthcare services at empanelled Level 2 dispensaries and Level 3 health centres are covered under the Primary Healthcare Fund without co-payment.

faq.question: How much is the monthly SHIF contribution in Kenya in 2026?
faq.answer: Salaried employees contribute 2.75% of gross monthly salary (with a minimum of KES 300/month and no upper cap), while non-salaried households contribute based on the SHA Means Testing Instrument (minimum KES 300/month).

faq.question: Is SHIF tax-deductible when calculating monthly KRA PAYE?
faq.answer: Yes. Under the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2024/2025, mandatory SHIF contributions (2.75% of gross pay) are fully tax-deductible before computing chargeable income for PAYE.

small-claims-calculator.notesTitle: Judiciary Small Claims Court (SCC) Rules & Filing Fees
overview: Established under the Small Claims Court Act (No. 2 of 2016), the Small Claims Court resolves civil and commercial disputes valued at KES 1,000,000 or less within a mandatory statutory timeline of 60 days from filing.
Proceedings are simplified, conducted in English or Kiswahili without strict technical rules of evidence, and allow mwananchi litigants to represent themselves without hiring an advocate.
howItWorks: Enter the total monetary value of your disputed claim (unpaid debt, withheld rent deposit, contract for sale of goods/services, or minor property damage).
The calculator checks whether the claim falls within the KES 1,000,000 statutory jurisdiction cap and determines the Judiciary e-Filing fee tier.
File your Statement of Claim online via the Judiciary e-Filing portal (efiling.court.go.ke) attaching M-Pesa statements, invoices, lease agreements, and your 7-day Demand Notice.

workedExample.title: Recovering an Unpaid KES 75,000 Business Invoice or Rent Deposit
workedExample.scenario: A supplier or former tenant is owed KES 75,000 after issuing a 7-day written demand notice that went unanswered.
steps: Claim amount of KES 75,000 is well below the KES 1,000,000 Small Claims Court cap.
Judiciary e-Filing fee for the KES 50,001 – KES 100,000 band is assessed on the e-Filing portal.
The Adjudicator hears and determines the matter within 60 days, issuing an enforceable decree.
workedExample.takeaway: Always send a written 7-day Demand Notice before filing so you can claim full filing costs alongside the principal debt.

complianceTips: Defamation, land title disputes, employment/labour disputes, and family/matrimonial matters are excluded from Small Claims Court jurisdiction.
Keep PDF copies of M-Pesa statements, WhatsApp acknowledgements of debt, and signed delivery notes ready for upload on efiling.court.go.ke.
notes: Maximum monetary jurisdiction of the Small Claims Court is KES 1,000,000 (Section 12 of the Small Claims Court Act).
Every claim must be heard and determined within 60 days from the date of filing.

faq.question: Do I need a lawyer to file a case in the Small Claims Court?
faq.answer: No. The Small Claims Court is specifically designed for self-representation using standard Statement of Claim forms on the Judiciary e-Filing portal, though parties may still opt to use an advocate.

faq.question: Can I sue my landlord for an unrefunded rent deposit in Small Claims Court?
faq.answer: Yes. Claims for refund of tenancy security deposits under KES 1,000,000 explicitly fall within Small Claims Court jurisdiction.

faq.question: Do I need a lawyer to file a case in Kenya's Small Claims Court?
faq.answer: No. Small Claims Court proceedings are designed for self-representation in English or Kiswahili without strict technical rules of evidence, though parties may choose to hire an advocate if they wish.

faq.question: How long does a Small Claims Court case take in Kenya?
faq.answer: Section 34 of the Small Claims Court Act mandates that every claim be heard and determined within 60 days from the date of filing.

ntsa-transfer-calculator.notesTitle: NTSA eCitizen Motor Vehicle Logbook Transfer Guidelines
overview: Motor vehicle and motorcycle ownership transfers in Kenya are processed digitally through the NTSA service portal on eCitizen under the Traffic Act (Cap 403).

Total transfer charges depend on the vehicle's engine capacity in cubic centimetres (cc) and combine the statutory NTSA transfer fee, motor vehicle purchase tax, official Copy of Records search fee, and eCitizen platform fee.
howItWorks: Choose between a Motor Vehicle or Motorcycle / Boda Boda and select the engine rating band (e.g., 1001–1200 cc, 1201–1500 cc, 1501–1700 cc, up to 3000+ cc).
View the exact itemized cost including NTSA Transfer Fee, Purchase Tax, Online Search Fee (KES 550), and eCitizen convenience fee (KES 50).
The seller initiates the transfer on eCitizen, uploads the scanned original logbook, and the buyer accepts the transfer in their own eCitizen account to receive the new logbook.

workedExample.title: Transferring a 1,500cc Toyota Fielder / Mazda Demio
workedExample.scenario: A buyer purchases a used 1,490cc car in Nairobi and wants to complete the eCitizen logbook transfer.
steps: Conduct an official NTSA Copy of Records search (KES 550) on eCitizen to verify the registered owner and confirm zero caveat/loan encumbrances.
Select the 1201–1500 cc band to compute the NTSA transfer fee and purchase tax.
Seller initiates logbook transfer on eCitizen; buyer accepts and pays the statutory fee.
workedExample.takeaway: Never release full purchase funds before conducting an official KES 550 NTSA Copy of Records search on eCitizen.

complianceTips: Under Section 9 of the Traffic Act, ownership transfer must be initiated within 14 days of sale.
Both seller and buyer must have active eCitizen accounts linked to their KRA PINs and National IDs.
notes: Fees are based on the Traffic Act (Cap 403) and NTSA gazetted motor vehicle transfer tariffs.
If a vehicle is co-owned with a bank or asset financier, the financier must first discharge their interest on the portal.

faq.question: How long does an NTSA logbook transfer take on eCitizen?
faq.answer: Once the seller initiates the transfer and the buyer accepts and pays on eCitizen, approval typically takes 3 to 7 working days before the new logbook is ready for collection.

faq.question: Who pays for the NTSA logbook transfer fee?
faq.answer: By market convention in Kenya, the buyer typically pays the eCitizen transfer fee upon accepting the transfer, unless agreed otherwise in the Sale Agreement.

faq.question: How long does an NTSA TIMS / eCitizen logbook transfer take?
faq.answer: Once both the seller and buyer accept the transfer on eCitizen TIMS and pay the statutory fee, approval typically takes 3 to 7 working days, after which the new logbook is printed for collection at the selected NTSA centre.

faq.question: What documents are required for a forced or deceased-owner vehicle transfer?
faq.answer: Forced transfers require a court order or auctioneer's certificate of sale, while deceased-owner transfers require a Confirmed Grant of Letters of Administration (or Probate) plus a certified copy of the death certificate.

boma-yangu-calculator.notesTitle: Boma Yangu (Affordable Housing Programme) & Tax Relief Rules
overview: The Boma Yangu Tenant Purchase Scheme (TPS) under the Affordable Housing Act 2024 enables Kenyan citizens to acquire Social, Affordable, and Affordable Middle-Class housing units with a 10% deposit and long-term fixed-interest repayments.
Employees and individuals saving or repaying towards an approved Affordable Housing scheme qualify for a 15% Affordable Housing Tax Relief on PAYE (up to KES 9,000 per month / KES 108,000 per year).
howItWorks: Select the Boma Yangu housing tier (Social Housing at 3%, Affordable Housing at 6%, or Affordable Market/Mortgage at 9%) and enter the unit purchase price.
The calculator computes the 10% required deposit, the 90% financed principal, the monthly TPS amortization payment, and the 15% PAYE tax relief.
Compare your gross monthly TPS installment against your net out-of-pocket monthly cost after KRA tax relief.

workedExample.title: 2-Bedroom Affordable Housing Unit at KES 2,400,000
workedExample.scenario: A contributor is allocated a KES 2,400,000 unit under the 6% p.a. Affordable Housing tier over a 25-year term.
steps: 10% Deposit required via Boma Yangu wallet: KES 240,000 (90% financed principal = KES 2,160,000).
Monthly TPS installment at 6% p.a. over 300 months is approximately KES 13,917.
15% Affordable Housing Tax Relief reduces monthly PAYE by KES 2,088, bringing net monthly cost to KES 11,829.
workedExample.takeaway: Claiming the 15% Affordable Housing Tax Relief through your employer's payroll reduces your effective monthly housing cost.

complianceTips: Register on bomayangu.go.ke or via *832# to track your mandatory 1.5% Affordable Housing Levy contributions and voluntary Boma Yangu savings.
Allocation strictly follows one-ID-one-unit rules under the Affordable Housing Act 2024.
notes: Interest rates and tenure limits reflect the Boma Yangu Tenant Purchase Scheme (TPS) guidelines (3% Social, 6% Affordable, 9% Market).
Affordable Housing Tax Relief is capped at 15% of contribution/repayment up to KES 9,000/month.

faq.question: How do I check my Boma Yangu savings balance?
faq.answer: Dial *832# on your phone or log in to bomayangu.go.ke using your National ID number to view both voluntary savings and statutory levy credits.

faq.question: What is the minimum deposit required for a Boma Yangu Affordable Housing unit?
faq.answer: Applicants save voluntarily through the Boma Yangu portal (PayBill 522522) toward a 10% deposit of the unit price, with flexible monthly tenant-purchase (TPS) repayment plans of up to 25–30 years.

faq.question: Are Affordable Housing Levy (1.5%) payroll deductions credited to my Boma Yangu savings?
faq.answer: No. The mandatory 1.5% Affordable Housing Levy is a statutory tax funding national housing construction; voluntary Boma Yangu deposits are tracked separately toward your personal home purchase deposit.

faq.question: What interest rates apply to Boma Yangu Tenant Purchase Schemes (TPS)?
faq.answer: Social Housing units attract 3% p.a. fixed interest, Affordable Housing units attract 6% p.a., and Affordable Middle-Class units attract 9% p.a. under the Affordable Housing Act.

rental-tax-calculator.notesTitle: Kenya Monthly Rental Income (7.5% MRI) vs. Net Graduated Income Tax Guide
overview: Under Section 6A of Kenya's Income Tax Act (Cap 470), resident landlords earning between KES 288,000 and KES 15,000,000 in annual gross residential rent qualify for the simplified 7.5% Monthly Rental Income (MRI) tax—payable monthly via itax.kra.go.ke by the 20th of the following month.

Turnover Tax (TOT) under Section 12C does not apply to rental income. Landlords with high deductible expenses (such as mortgage interest, repairs, insurance, and caretaker salaries) may elect in writing to the Commissioner to be taxed on net rental profit under normal graduated Income Tax rates instead of gross 7.5% MRI.
howItWorks: Enter your gross monthly residential rent collected in KES.
Enter your allowable monthly property expenses (mortgage interest, repairs, management fees, insurance, land rates).
Compare the simplified 7.5% gross MRI obligation against Net Graduated Income Tax on your annual net rental profit.
File your monthly MRI return (or annual net rental income return) via KRA iTax at itax.kra.go.ke.

workedExample.title: Landlord Collecting KES 85,000 Monthly Residential Rent
workedExample.scenario: A landlord collects KES 85,000 in gross residential rent for October 2026.
steps: Gross monthly rent = KES 85,000 (Annualized = KES 1,020,000, within the KES 288k–15M MRI threshold).
Return and payment must be submitted on KRA iTax by November 20th to avoid the KES 2,000 late-filing penalty.
workedExample.takeaway: If no rent was collected in a given month, file a Nil MRI return on iTax before the 20th to avoid automatic late-filing penalties.

complianceTips: File and pay Monthly Rental Income (7.5% MRI) on itax.kra.go.ke on or before the 20th day of the following month—late filing attracts a KES 2,000/month penalty plus 1% monthly interest.
Landlords electing Net Graduated Tax must keep audited/verifiable receipts for all mortgage interest, repairs, and property management expenses.
notes: MRI rate was reduced from 10% to 7.5% of gross residential rent effective January 1, 2024.
Commercial property rent does not qualify for 7.5% residential MRI and is taxed under normal corporate/individual income tax rules.

faq.question: Can I deduct repair costs or mortgage interest under the 7.5% MRI tax?
faq.answer: No. The 7.5% MRI tax is charged on gross residential rent without expense deductions. However, a landlord may write to the KRA Commissioner to opt out of MRI and be taxed on net rental profit under standard income tax rates.

faq.question: What is the Monthly Rental Income (MRI) tax rate in Kenya in 2026?
faq.answer: Resident landlords earning between KES 288,000 and KES 15,000,000 per year in gross residential rent pay a flat 7.5% Monthly Rental Income (MRI) tax on gross rent collected, filed on iTax by the 20th of the following month.

faq.question: Can landlords deduct repairs or mortgage interest under the 7.5% MRI regime?
faq.answer: No. The 7.5% MRI tax is a final tax calculated on gross rent without expense deductions. Landlords with high maintenance or mortgage costs may elect in writing to be taxed under the regular corporate/individual income tax regime instead.

faq.question: What is the penalty for late filing of Monthly Rental Income tax?
faq.answer: Late filing attracts a penalty of KES 2,000 (individuals) or KES 20,000 (companies) or 5% of tax due (whichever is higher), plus 5% late payment penalty and 1% monthly interest.

landlord-tenant-rights.notesTitle: Kenyan Tenancy Law, Illegal Lock-Outs & Deposit Recovery
overview: Kenyan residential tenancies are governed by the Rent Restriction Act (Cap 296), the Distress for Rent Act (Cap 293), the Land Act (2012), and Small Claims Court case law.

A landlord or managing agent cannot lawfully lock a tenant's door, disconnect water or electricity, seize household goods without a licensed Court Auctioneer's proclamation, or withhold a security deposit for normal wear-and-tear repainting.
howItWorks: Review the statutory checklist of unlawful landlord actions versus lawful security deposit deductions.
Fill in your name, the landlord or agency name, house/unit number, withheld deposit amount, and vacating date in the Statutory Demand Notice Generator.
Tap 'Share / Send Demand Notice' to send the formal 7-day demand notice via WhatsApp or email before filing in the Small Claims Court.

workedExample.title: Recovering a KES 45,000 Security Deposit Withheld for 'Repainting'
workedExample.scenario: A tenant vacates an apartment after 2 years with zero utility arrears, but the caretaker withholds KES 45,000 claiming routine wall repainting costs.
steps: Take timestamped handover photos/video of the clean apartment and KPLC/water meter readings on move-out day.
Issue the 7-Day Statutory Demand Notice generated by this tool citing Small Claims Court precedents on fair wear and tear.
If unpaid after 7 days, file a claim on efiling.court.go.ke for full recovery within 60 days.
workedExample.takeaway: Standard wear-and-tear repainting between tenants is the landlord's statutory burden unless the tenant caused physical structural damage.

complianceTips: Always obtain a signed move-in and move-out inspection checklist and clearance receipts for water, service charge, and KPLC tokens.
Distress for rent (seizing goods for arrears) can only be executed by a licensed Auctioneer after issuing a mandatory 14-day proclamation notice.
notes: Security deposits remain the tenant's money held in trust and must be refunded upon vacating once utility bills and physical damages beyond fair wear and tear are cleared.
Locking a tenant out without a court eviction order is an offence under the Rent Restriction Act.

faq.question: Is a landlord allowed to lock my house or switch off water for late rent?
faq.answer: No. Kenyan courts have consistently ruled that locking a tenant out or disconnecting water/electricity is unlawful self-help and violates constitutional and statutory tenancy protections.

faq.question: Can a Kenyan landlord lock out a residential tenant or seize furniture without a court order?
faq.answer: No. Illegal lockouts, disconnecting water/electricity, or seizing household goods without a licensed auctioneer acting under the Distress for Rent Act (Cap 293) is unlawful and actionable before the Rent Restriction Tribunal.

faq.question: How long should a landlord take to refund a security deposit after vacating?
faq.answer: While the exact timeline is governed by the tenancy agreement, standard Kenyan practice and tribunal rulings require landlords to inspect the premises and refund the security deposit (less itemized, receipted damage repairs) within 14 to 30 days of handover.

faq.question: Which tribunal handles commercial shop leases versus residential disputes?
faq.answer: Commercial controlled tenancies (less than 5 years or lacking a written agreement) are handled by the Business Premises Rent Tribunal (BPRT), whereas residential disputes under statutory limits go to the Rent Restriction Tribunal or Small Claims Court.

Statutory minimum wages vary across three geographic tiers: Cities (Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, and Eldoret — KES 18,047/month floor), Former Municipalities & Town Councils (Thika, Nyeri, Kisii, Malindi, Kakamega, Machakos — KES 16,650/month), and All Other Rural Areas (KES 11,482/month).

faq.question: Must I register my househelp for SHA and NSSF in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Kenyan labour and social security laws, every employer of a domestic worker is required to remit monthly NSSF and SHA contributions.

faq.question: Are domestic workers in Kenya entitled to paid annual leave and maternity leave?
faq.answer: Yes. Under the Employment Act (Cap 226), every domestic worker who completes 12 consecutive months of service is entitled to at least 21 working days of paid annual leave, 1 rest day per week, and 3 months paid maternity leave (or 2 weeks paternity leave).

faq.question: Do employers have to remit NSSF and SHA for house helps and gardeners?
faq.answer: Yes. Employers of domestic workers are legally required to register as employers and remit monthly NSSF Tier I/II contributions and 2.75% SHIF contributions (minimum KES 300/month) by the 9th of each month.

faq.question: Does the statutory minimum wage differ between Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, and rural areas?
faq.answer: Yes. Kenya's Regulation of Wages Order sets three geographic tiers: Cities (Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu), Former Municipalities & Urban Councils, and All Other Areas (rural), with higher minimum wages in cities.

faq.question: Why does KRA disallow business expenses that lack an eTIMS invoice?
faq.answer: Under the Finance Act and KRA's 2026 automated eTIMS cross-matching rules, every deductible business expense must be backed by a valid eTIMS-transmitted tax invoice bearing the buyer's KRA PIN. faq.question: Which expenses are legally exempt from KRA eTIMS invoicing?

faq.question: How does Buyer-Initiated (Reverse) eTIMS invoicing work for small suppliers?

complianceTips: ODPC determinations include KES 700,000 (Alston v Liquid Telecom, exit call recording) and KES 500,000 (Kirima v Solar Panda, unconsented staff photo).

faq.question: How long must Kenyan employers keep employee payroll and HR records?
faq.answer: Under the Kenya Employment Act (Cap 226) and Tax Procedures Act, employers must retain employee contracts, payroll, PAYE, NSSF, and SHA records for at least 5 years (and up to 7 years for tax and statutory audit defense), while unsuccessful job applicant CVs should be purged once the recruitment window closes unless explicit consent is given.

faq.question: What are the penalties for non-compliance with the Kenya Data Protection Act (2019)?
faq.answer: The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) can issue enforcement notices and administrative fines of up to KES 5,000,000 or 1% of annual turnover (whichever is lower) for unlawful retention, unauthorized disclosure, or failure to register as a data controller/processor.

faq.question: When is a Kenyan business legally required to register with the ODPC?
faq.answer: Mandatory registration applies to any organization with annual turnover above KES 5 million or more than 10 employees, as well as all entities in sensitive sectors (healthcare, education, financial services, hospitality, real estate, and direct marketing) regardless of size.

faq.question: What should an employer do when a retention period expires?
faq.answer: Once the statutory retention period ends and no legal dispute or KRA audit is pending, personal records must be securely anonymized or permanently destroyed, and the disposal logged in your ODPC retention register.

notes: Section 63 of the Data Protection Act (2019) caps administrative penalty notices at the lower of KES 5,000,000 or 1% of annual turnover.
Registration with odpc.go.ke is mandatory for organizations with 10+ employees or annual turnover above KES 5,000,000 (or any entity processing sensitive personal data).

faq.question: When do EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) geolocation rules take effect for Kenyan coffee?
faq.answer: Under EU Regulation 2023/1115 (as amended), large operators and traders must comply by 30 December 2026, while micro and small enterprises have until 30 June 2027. Every coffee shipment to the EU must prove plots were not deforested after 31 December 2020.

faq.question: When do I need a closed GPS polygon versus a single GPS point under EUDR?
faq.answer: Smallholder coffee farms under 4 hectares (< 4 ha) may submit either a single WGS84 latitude/longitude point or a polygon. Any plot of 4 hectares or larger (>= 4 ha) strictly requires a closed GeoJSON polygon with at least 4 vertices where the first and last coordinates match.

faq.question: Why does RFC 7946 GeoJSON use [longitude, latitude] ordering?
faq.answer: The EU TRACES NT portal validates uploaded files against the RFC 7946 GeoJSON specification, which mandates [longitude, latitude] order (e.g., [36.95, -0.4167] for Nyeri) in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) with at least 6 decimal places of precision.

faq.question: What happens if my declared plot area differs from the computed polygon area?
faq.answer: EU TRACES validates the actual polygon geometry rather than the self-reported acreage. If the computed polygon area crosses the 4-hectare threshold or differs significantly from the cooperative register, re-walk the farm perimeter with a <10m GNSS receiver before exporting.

notes: EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) requires polygon GeoJSON boundaries for coffee/cocoa/rubber/timber plots above 4 hectares (and single-point coordinates for plots ≤ 4 ha) in WGS84 (EPSG:4326).
Polygon rings must be closed (first coordinate equal to last coordinate) and follow RFC 7946 counter-clockwise exterior ring winding.

faq.question: How does KRA iCMS calculate cascading import taxes on commercial cargo?
faq.answer: KRA computes Customs Value (CIF = FOB + Freight + 1.5% Insurance), then applies EAC CET Import Duty (0%, 10%, 25%, or 35%) on CIF, 16% VAT on (CIF + Import Duty + Excise), plus 2.5% Import Declaration Fee (IDF) and 2.0% Railway Development Levy (RDL) on CIF.

faq.question: Why are China-to-Kenya consolidators often cheaper for small shipments?
faq.answer: Consolidators pool multiple SME orders into shared containers and quote an all-in rate per CBM (typically KES 60,000–70,000/CBM by sea) or per kg by air (KES 1,500–1,900/kg) that bundles freight, clearing, and consolidated customs clearance—avoiding fixed KES 30,000+ minimum clearing agent and port handling charges on small volumes.

faq.question: When is independent KRA iCMS clearing better than using a consolidator?
faq.answer: Independent clearing usually wins for high-volume shipments (3+ CBM or full containers), 0%-duty industrial machinery/raw materials, or VAT-registered businesses that need an official KRA iCMS Entry C17B to claim 16% input VAT and eTIMS-compliant cost of goods sold.

16% VAT cascades on (CIF + Import Duty), while 2.5% IDF and 2.0% RDL apply directly on CIF.

faq.question: How does the Social Health Authority (SHA) 30-day statutory submission window work?

faq.question: Does SHA cover both primary healthcare (PHC) and inpatient SHIF benefits?
faq.answer: Yes. faq.question: Why are Kenyan tenders frequently disqualified at the Preliminary Evaluation stage?

faq.question: How does Kenya's AGPO 30% reservation preference work?

faq.question: How does KJSEA place Grade 9 learners into Senior School pathways under CBC?
faq.answer: The Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) combines School-Based Assessments (SBA) from Grades 7–8 (40% total weight, with 20% from KPSEA/lower SBA) and the summative Grade 9 KNEC exam (60% weight) to place learners into STEM, Social Sciences, or Arts & Sports Science.

faq.question: What are the three Senior School pathways in Kenya's CBC Grade 10–12 system?
faq.answer: The three KICD pathways are: (1) STEM (Pure Sciences, Applied Sciences, Technical Studies), (2) Social Sciences (Humanities & Business Studies, Languages & Literature), and (3) Arts & Sports Science (Performing Arts, Visual Arts, Sports Science).

faq.question: How do KJSEA performance levels map to points?
faq.answer: KNEC reports KJSEA performance across four core bands subdivided into 8 levels: Exceeding Expectations (EE1 = 8, EE2 = 7), Meeting Expectations (ME1 = 6, ME2 = 5), Approaching Expectations (AE1 = 4, AE2 = 3), and Below Expectations (BE1 = 2, BE2 = 1).

faq.question: Can a student switch Senior School pathways after Grade 10 placement?
faq.answer: Limited transfers are permitted within the first term of Grade 10 subject to school capacity, Ministry of Education guidelines, and whether the learner meets the prerequisite subject performance levels for the target track.

notes: Senior School (Grade 10–12) placement blends 20% KPSEA (Grade 6), 20% Junior School SBA (Grades 7–8), and 60% Grade 9 KJSEA summative score.
Learners are matched into STEM, Social Sciences, or Arts & Sports Science pathways based on weighted performance and subject cluster strength.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Grade 9 Learner Targeting the STEM Pathway
workedExample.scenario: A Grade 9 candidate scores 78% in KPSEA, 82% in Junior School SBA, and 80% in KJSEA:
steps: Weighted KPSEA contribution (20% × 78): 15.6 points
Weighted SBA contribution (20% × 82): 16.4 points
Weighted KJSEA contribution (60% × 80): 48.0 points
Composite Placement Score: 80.0 / 100 — qualifies strongly for STEM (Pure & Applied Sciences) Senior School placement.
workedExample.takeaway: Consistent Grades 7–8 School-Based Assessments contribute 20% of final placement, rewarding steady classroom project work.

ardhisasa-cad-title-auditor.notesTitle: Ardhisasa GIS/CAD Topology & Root-of-Title Due Diligence
overview: 85%–87% of buildings in rapidly urbanizing Kenyan zones lack full compliance/deformation sign-offs, and Ardhisasa rejects sectional CAD/GIS plans with unclosed polygons or datum errors.
howItWorks: Paste parcel beacon coordinates to validate polygon closure, self-intersections, and computed area tolerance.
Complete the Root-of-Title (Kenya Gazette succession, Ndung'u Report) and NCA/EBK/BORAQS/ISK structural sign-off checklist.
complianceTips: Verify Cassini-Soldner to ARC1960 / UTM Zone 37S datum shifts before submitting sectional mutation plans on Ardhisasa.

faq.question: What causes a parcel survey plan to fail Ardhisasa geospatial validation?
faq.answer: Common rejection reasons include unclosed beacon traverses (misclosure exceeding Survey of Kenya linear tolerance), self-intersecting boundary lines, mismatched UTM Zone 37S / Arc 1960 vs. WGS84 datum coordinates, or area discrepancies exceeding statutory tolerance.

faq.question: What is the difference between a Title Deed search on Ardhisasa and a physical green card search?
faq.answer: For converted Nairobi and digitized registry blocks, official land searches are conducted online via Ardhisasa (ardhisasa.lands.go.ke) for KES 500. For counties not yet migrated onto Ardhisasa, buyers must still conduct an official search at the respective County Land Registry and verify the physical green card.

faq.question: Which professional bodies must sign off on a compliant Kenyan building & land project?
faq.answer: Licensed land surveyors (ISK / Survey of Kenya) certify beacon coordinates and mutations; BORAQS registers Architects and Quantity Surveyors; EBK registers Structural and Civil Engineers; and NCA registers the project site and contractor before construction begins.

faq.question: Does the Ardhisasa CAD Title Auditor replace a licensed surveyor?
faq.answer: No. It is a pre-validation engineering tool to catch beacon closure errors, self-intersections, and root-of-title checklist gaps early—formal mutation forms and Rim/FR plans must still be signed by a licensed Kenyan surveyor.

notes: Polygon area is computed via the Shoelace formula on UTM Zone 37S (WGS84) Easting/Northing coordinates in meters.
A valid closed cadastral parcel must repeat its starting beacon coordinate as the final row (closure error < 0.05m) and match the declared title area within Survey Regulations tolerance.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Auditing a 2,000 m² (0.20 ha) Parcel Before Ardhisasa Transfer
workedExample.scenario: A licensed surveyor or buyer pastes 5 UTM Zone 37S beacon coordinate pairs (4 corners + closing point) for a 2,000 m² title:
steps: Computed Shoelace polygon area matches 2,000.0 m² (0.2000 ha) with 0.00% area variance.
Polygon closure error is 0.00 m (Closed), passing geometric topology checks.
Complete all 6 Root-of-Title checks (Ardhisasa official search, Green Card history, Kenya Gazette, Ndung'u report, datum check, and NCA/EBK sign-offs).
workedExample.takeaway: Verifying beacon geometry and Root-of-Title history before paying a deposit prevents costly Ardhisasa rejection and double-allocation disputes.

school-fee-cap-auditor.notesTitle: MoE Special Gazette Notice No. 1449 (Feb 6, 2026) Senior School Fee Caps
overview: Under Special Gazette Notice No. 1449 dated February 6, 2026, the Ministry of Education enforces strict annual parent fee ceilings for all public Senior Schools in Kenya: KES 0 for Public Day schools (backed by KES 22,244 GoK capitation), KES 53,554 for Cluster 1 / Major Urban Boarding schools, KES 40,535 for Other Public Boarding schools, and KES 12,790 for Special Needs Boarding schools (supplemented by KES 57,974 GoK capitation).

Schools must collect fees strictly along the statutory 50% (Term 1), 30% (Term 2), and 20% (Term 3) schedule and are prohibited from adding unauthorized levies such as remedial tuition, teacher motivation fees, or tied uniform monopolies.
howItWorks: Select the public Senior School category (Day, Cluster 1 / Major Urban Boarding, Other Boarding, or Special Needs Boarding).
Enter the school's quoted annual or per-term fee structure and toggle any extra levies listed on the admission or fee circular.
Review the exact KES overcharge above the Gazette Notice 1449 ceiling, term-by-term legal limits (50/30/20), and flagged illegal levies.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Auditing an Extra-County Boarding School Circular
workedExample.scenario: A County/Extra-County boarding school outside major urban towns quotes KES 56,500 per year including KES 6,000 remedial tuition and KES 4,500 bus fund:

complianceTips: Request written County Education Board (CEB) authorization before paying any school development or bus levy.

notes: Annual parent ceilings under Gazette Notice No. 1449 (Feb 6, 2026): Day KES 0, Cluster 1 Urban Boarding KES 53,554, Other Boarding KES 40,535, Special Needs Boarding KES 12,790.
Report unlawful levies or tied uniform mandates to the Ministry of Education hotline (0800 720 071) or the Commission on Administrative Justice (CAJ).

faq.question: What is the maximum legal school fee for public boarding Senior Schools in Kenya in 2026?
faq.answer: Under Special Gazette Notice No. 1449 (February 6, 2026), Cluster 1 / Major Urban Boarding schools (Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, Eldoret, Nyeri, Thika) are capped at KES 53,554 per year, while Other Public Boarding schools are capped at KES 40,535 per year.

faq.question: How are public Senior School fees split across Term 1, Term 2, and Term 3?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Education mandates a 50% / 30% / 20% payment ratio: 50% in Term 1, 30% in Term 2, and 20% in Term 3.

faq.question: Can a public school force parents to buy uniforms only from the school canteen?
faq.answer: No. Ministry of Education circulars expressly bar public schools from monopolizing uniform sales; schools may specify colours and design standards, but parents are free to buy uniforms from any accredited tailor or shop.

cooking-fuel-comparator.notesTitle: Kenyan Household Cooking Fuel Economics & Electric Pressure Cooker (EPC) Payback
overview: Cooking energy is one of the largest recurring monthly expenses for Kenyan households, yet fuel cost comparisons often overlook thermal efficiency. While charcoal (KES 180/debe or KES 2,800/bag) and kerosene (EPRA Nairobi KES 191.38/L) lose over half their energy as waste heat, an Electric Pressure Cooker (EPC) retains pressurized steam at ~85% efficiency.

Using KPLC domestic tariffs (~KES 24.50/kWh) and TotalEnergies LPG refill benchmarks (KES 1,570 for 6 kg; KES 3,530 for 13 kg), this comparator models exact per-dish and monthly fuel spend across Kenyan staple meals—githeri, dry beans, ugali & sukuma wiki, rice & stew, and chapati.
howItWorks: Select your household's weekly meal frequency for githeri, dry beans, ugali/sukuma, rice/stew, and chapati.
Adjust local prices for 6 kg/13 kg LPG refills, charcoal debe/bag, EPRA kerosene, KPLC electricity per kWh, and EPC purchase cost (default KES 9,500).
Inspect per-dish KES cost, monthly fuel totals, and exact months to recover the cost of an EPC.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Boiling 1 kg Dry Githeri Across 4 Kenyan Fuels
workedExample.scenario: Comparing energy cost to boil 1 kg of dry maize and beans (githeri) on EPC vs LPG vs Charcoal vs Kerosene:
steps: Electric Pressure Cooker (EPC): ~0.48 kWh × KES 24.50 = KES 11.76 (45 minutes).
Charcoal jiko: ~1.35 kg × KES 40/kg = KES 54.00 (180 minutes).
LPG 13 kg cylinder: ~0.28 kg × KES 271.54/kg = KES 76.03.
Kerosene stove: ~0.42 L × KES 191.38/L = KES 80.38.
workedExample.takeaway: Switching heavy-boil dishes like githeri and dry beans from charcoal or LPG to an EPC cuts per-meal fuel cost by 75%–85% and pays back a KES 9,500 EPC in roughly 4–6 months.

complianceTips: Soaking dry maize and beans overnight reduces cooking time and energy use by 20%–30% across all fuels.
Always buy LPG refills from licensed EPRA-compliant dealers and verify the cylinder seal before leaving.
notes: Benchmarks use TotalEnergies 2026 LPG (6 kg KES 1,570; 13 kg KES 3,530), EPRA Nairobi Kerosene (KES 191.38/L), Charcoal (KES 180/debe, KES 2,800/bag), and KPLC Domestic (KES 24.50/kWh).
Hybrid cooking—using an EPC for heavy boiling/stews and LPG for quick frying/ugali—typically delivers the lowest total monthly household bill.

faq.question: Is an Electric Pressure Cooker (EPC) really cheaper than LPG gas in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes for boiling and stewing dishes. Cooking githeri or dry beans in an insulated EPC uses roughly 0.36–0.48 kWh (KES 9–12 on KPLC domestic tariffs), compared to KES 55–80 on LPG or charcoal.

faq.question: How long does it take for an EPC to pay for itself in a Kenyan household?
faq.answer: A typical KES 9,500 EPC saves KES 1,500–2,500 per month for a family of four cooking beans, githeri, and stews regularly, achieving full payback in 4 to 6 months.

faq.question: Does KPLC Lifeline vs Domestic tariff change EPC cooking costs?
faq.answer: Yes. Households staying within the KPLC Lifeline band (0–30 kWh/month) pay a lower effective per-kWh rate than the standard KES 24.50/kWh Domestic rate, making EPC cooking even cheaper.

auctioneer-fee-shield.notesTitle: Auctioneers Act (Cap 526) Fourth Schedule Fee Ceilings & Repossession Protections
overview: Under the Auctioneers Act (Cap 526) and the Auctioneers Rules (Fourth Schedule), licensed auctioneers in Kenya are strictly bound by statutory fee scales for attendance, proclamation, and sale commissions on both movable and immovable property. Arbitrary demands for inflated 'storage', 'transport', or 'standby' charges outside court-taxed bills are unlawful.

The Act also enforces mandatory notice periods—7 days after proclamation of movable goods, 14 days for rent distress sales, and 45 days' redemption notice before auctioning immovable land—and requires a valid annual Auctioneers Licensing Board (ALB) practicing certificate.
howItWorks: Choose whether the enforcement involves movable goods (vehicles, household items, shop stock) or immovable property (land/buildings).
Enter the principal debt or proclaimed asset value and the auctioneer's demanded fee.
Compare the demanded amount against the exact Fourth Schedule statutory cap and run the 5-point illegality red-flag check.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Checking a Movable Goods Attachment on a KES 250,000 Debt
workedExample.scenario: An auctioneer proclaims household goods for a KES 250,000 debt and demands KES 85,000 in fees:
steps: Fourth Schedule attendance fee (movable): KES 4,000; Proclamation fee: KES 2,000.
Statutory commission: 10% on first KES 100,000 (KES 10,000) + 5% on remaining KES 150,000 (KES 7,500) = KES 17,500.
Total statutory ceiling before court-taxed disbursements: KES 23,500 — flagging KES 61,500 in excessive demand.
workedExample.takeaway: If an auctioneer's bill exceeds the Fourth Schedule, you can file a formal Bill of Costs taxation challenge in court and report misconduct to the Auctioneers Licensing Board.

complianceTips: Always demand to inspect the auctioneer's current-year ALB practicing certificate and the signed Court Warrant or Letter of Instruction.
Under Section 44 of the Civil Procedure Act, basic bedding, clothing, cooking utensils, and essential tools of trade are exempt from attachment.
notes: Movable commission tiers: 10% up to KES 100,000, 5% on the next KES 900,000, and 2.5% on any excess above KES 1,000,000.
Immovable commission tiers: 10% up to KES 600,000, 5% between KES 600,001 and KES 3,000,000, and 2% above KES 3,000,000.

faq.question: Can an auctioneer carry away my household goods on the very day they arrive?
faq.answer: No. For movable property, the Auctioneers Rules require a formal Proclamation Notice giving the debtor at least 7 days to settle or challenge the debt before goods can be removed for sale.

faq.question: What are the statutory attendance and proclamation fees under Cap 526?
faq.answer: Under the Fourth Schedule, standard attendance fees are KES 4,000 for movable property and KES 8,000 for immovable property, plus KES 2,000 for proclamation.

faq.question: Where do I report an unlicensed or abusive auctioneer in Kenya?
faq.answer: You can file a formal complaint with the Auctioneers Licensing Board (ALB) under the Judiciary of Kenya and apply to the Magistrates' or High Court to tax down unlawful fees.

succession-cap160-calculator.notesTitle: Law of Succession Act (Cap 160) Intestate Distribution & Probate Fee Guide
overview: When a Kenyan citizen passes away without a valid written or oral will (intestate), the Law of Succession Act (Cap 160) governs how net property is shared among surviving spouses, children, parents, and siblings. Sections 35, 38, 39, and 40 establish gender-equal inheritance rights for both sons and daughters—whether married or unmarried.

Before any bank account, SACCO share, vehicle, or land title can be transferred, administrators must obtain Letters of Administration Intestate from the High Court or Magistrate's Court (jurisdiction up to KES 20M) and wait 6 months for Confirmation of Grant.
howItWorks: Select the family structure (Section 35 monogamous with spouse & children, Section 38 children only, Section 39 no spouse/children, or Section 40 polygamous houses).
Enter the net estate value and number of surviving spouses/children per house.
Review each beneficiary's statutory share, estimated Advocates (Remuneration) Order (ARO) probate fees + 16% VAT, and the P&A filing checklist.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Section 40 Polygamous Intestate Estate of KES 12,000,000
workedExample.scenario: A deceased man leaves 2 houses: House 1 has a surviving wife + 3 children (4 units); House 2 has a surviving wife + 1 child (2 units):
steps: Under Section 40, each surviving wife counts as an extra unit alongside her children: total units = 4 + 2 = 6 units.
House 1 receives 4/6 (66.67%) = KES 8,000,000; House 2 receives 2/6 (33.33%) = KES 4,000,000.
Within each house, the surviving wife holds a life interest in her house's share alongside her children under Section 35.
workedExample.takeaway: Section 40 prevents arbitrary disinheritance by tying every house's share strictly to its unit count.

complianceTips: Never sell or subdivide a deceased person's land before Confirmation of Grant—doing so is criminal intermeddling under Section 45 of Cap 160.
Obtain the Area Chief's Letter listing every surviving child (including married daughters and children born outside marriage) to avoid grant revocation.
notes: Statutory Kenya Gazette publication carries a mandatory 30-day objection period before the initial Grant of Letters of Administration issues.
Confirmation of Grant (Form 108) is ordinarily applied for 6 months after the grant is issued, unless urgent partial confirmation is granted by the court.

faq.question: Do married daughters inherit equally with sons under Kenyan law?
faq.answer: Yes. Under Sections 35, 38, and 40 of the Law of Succession Act (Cap 160) and Article 27 of the Constitution of Kenya (2010), all children—sons and daughters, married or unmarried—inherit equally.

faq.question: What does a surviving spouse's 'life interest' under Section 35 mean?
faq.answer: A surviving spouse is entitled to personal and household effects absolutely and holds a life interest (right to use and draw income) over the net residue in trust for the children; they cannot sell immovable land without court consent or beneficiaries' agreement.

faq.question: How long does an uncontested succession case take in Kenya?
faq.answer: An uncontested intestate succession typically takes 8 to 12 months: ~2–3 months for filing, 30-day Kenya Gazette notice, and initial Grant, followed by the statutory 6-month waiting period before Confirmation of Grant.

duka-hustle-ubp-calculator.notesTitle: Kenyan Micro-Retail Break-Even, Spoilage & 2026 Nairobi UBP Guide
overview: Small Kenyan hustles—neighbourhood dukas, mama mboga stalls, mitumba bale traders, and kinyozis/salons—often appear profitable on daily cash flow while quietly losing money to stock spoilage, unbudgeted rent, and annual County Unified Business Permit (UBP) renewals.

This calculator combines 2026 Nairobi City County UBP tiers (Kiosk <5 m² KES 3,500–4,000 + KES 200 application fee, Mini Shop KES 5,000, Small Trader KES 10,000, Medium Shop KES 15,000) with real gross-margin and spoilage drag modeling to reveal your exact daily break-even sales target.
howItWorks: Choose a hustle preset (Neighbourhood Duka, Mama Mboga, Mitumba Bale Trader, or Kinyozi/Salon) or customize your own costs.
Select your County UBP tier, monthly rent, utilities, gross margin %, and realistic stock spoilage/dead-stock %.
See the exact daily and monthly revenue required to break even after amortized UBP, rent, and spoilage losses.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: Mama Mboga Stall with 12% Fresh-Produce Spoilage
workedExample.scenario: A fresh produce vendor pays KES 4,000/month rent, KES 1,000 utilities, KES 3,700 annual Kiosk UBP + app fee (~KES 308/mo), with 32% gross margin and 12% spoilage:
steps: Total monthly fixed overhead (rent + utilities + amortized UBP): KES 5,308.
Effective net contribution margin after 12% produce spoilage: 32% - 12% = 20%.
Monthly break-even sales: KES 5,308 / 0.20 = KES 26,540 (~KES 1,021/day over 26 trading days).
workedExample.takeaway: Cutting fresh-produce spoilage from 12% to 6% drops your daily break-even sales target by nearly a quarter.

complianceTips: Renew your County UBP before March 31 each year via Nairobi Services (nairobiservices.go.ke) to avoid late-renewal penalties.
Food handlers (dukas selling unpacked food, eateries, mama mboga) also require a 6-month Public Health Food Handler's Certificate.
notes: 2026 Nairobi UBP base tiers: Kiosk (<5 m²) KES 3,500–4,000, Mini Shop KES 5,000, Small Trader KES 10,000, Medium Shop KES 15,000, each plus KES 200 application fee.
Keep a separate M-Pesa Till or business wallet so personal household withdrawals do not mask operating losses.

faq.question: How much is a Nairobi Unified Business Permit (UBP) for a small duka or kiosk in 2026?
faq.answer: In 2026, Nairobi City County charges KES 3,500–4,000 for a kiosk under 5 m², KES 5,000 for a mini shop, KES 10,000 for a small trader, and KES 15,000 for a medium shop, plus a KES 200 application fee.

faq.question: Why does spoilage matter so much for mama mboga and mitumba businesses?
faq.answer: Spoiled tomatoes or unsellable Grade-C mitumba pieces directly reduce your realized gross margin. A 10% spoilage rate on a 30% margin business cuts your effective profit cushion by one-third.

faq.question: Do small dukas need to pay KRA Turnover Tax (TOT) or eTIMS?
faq.answer: Businesses with annual gross turnover between KES 1,000,000 and KES 25,000,000 are subject to KRA Turnover Tax (1.5%) and eTIMS invoicing; micro-traders below KES 1M/year are exempt from TOT.

funeral-harambee-planner.notesTitle: Kenya Funeral Costing, Morgue Tariffs (KUFH/KUTRRH 2026) & Harambee Pledge Guide
overview: Planning a Kenyan funeral under emotional pressure often leads to runaway mortuary bills and painful last-minute deficits when WhatsApp/M-Pesa harambee pledges fall short of actual cash collected. Public referral funeral homes like Kenyatta University Funeral Home (KUFH) / KUTRRH charge transparent tiered rates: KES 5,500 adult (KES 3,500 child) for 0–24h transit, KES 10,000 adult (KES 6,000 child) flat for Days 1–10, and KES 1,000/day adult (KES 700/day child) from Day 11 onward.
This planner estimates total morgue charges by days held, lets committees customize coffin, hearse, tent, and catering tiers, and models realistic cash-in-hand using a pledge-realization factor.

Pick a Modest, Standard, or Executive funeral tier and adjust line items (coffin, hearse, tents/chairs, catering, PA/flowers).

workedExample.title: Worked Example: 14-Day Adult Morgue Stay & Standard Funeral Budget
workedExample.scenario: A family plans burial 14 days after admission at KUFH/KUTRRH tariffs with a Standard funeral budget:
steps: Morgue fee: KES 10,000 (Days 1–10 flat) + 4 extra days × KES 1,000 = KES 14,000.

Designate two independent treasurers and share daily M-Pesa statement screenshots with the funeral committee for transparency.
notes: Morgue benchmarks reflect KUFH/KUTRRH 2026 schedules: Transit 0–24h KES 5,500 (child KES 3,500); Days 1–10 flat KES 10,000 (child KES 6,000); Day 11+ KES 1,000/day (child KES 700/day).
Private funeral homes in Nairobi and Mombasa typically charge 1.8×–3× public referral mortuary rates.

faq.question: How much does Kenyatta University Funeral Home (KUFH) charge per day?
faq.answer: Under the 2026 benchmark schedule, KUFH charges KES 5,500 for 0–24h transit, a flat KES 10,000 for Days 1–10 (KES 6,000 for children), and KES 1,000 per day from Day 11 onward (KES 700/day for children).

faq.question: What percentage of funeral harambee pledges actually convert to cash in Kenya?
faq.answer: Funeral committees typically realize 70% to 80% of pledged amounts before burial day; planning with a 75% realization buffer avoids last-minute shortfalls.

faq.question: What documents are required to clear a body from a Kenyan mortuary?
faq.answer: You need the official Burial Permit, copies of the deceased's and next-of-kin's National IDs, the Area Chief's letter (for rural burials), and the paid morgue clearance receipt.

rainwater-tank-sizer.notesTitle: Kenya 47-County Roof Rainwater Harvesting & Tank Sizing Engineering Guide
overview: Every millimetre of rainfall landing on 1 square metre of roof yields 1 litre of gross rainwater. Across Kenya's 47 counties, seasonal rainfall varies dramatically—from ~250 mm/year in arid Turkana and Mandera to 1,350–1,400 mm/year in Kericho, Kisii, and Kakamega—split primarily between the March–April–May (MAM) long rains and October–November–December (OND) short rains.

By combining your county's MAM/OND rainfall, roof plan area, material runoff coefficient (mabati 0.90, tile 0.85, concrete 0.80), and household daily consumption, this tool calculates harvestable litres and matches you to Kenyan retail tank sizes (1,500 L to 10,000 L).
howItWorks: Select your county from all 47 Kenyan counties to load local MAM, OND, annual rainfall, and typical dry-spell length.
Enter your horizontal roof area (m²), roof material (Mabati, Tile, or Concrete), and household daily water demand (litres/day).
View seasonal harvestable litres, recommended tank capacity, days of dry-spell autonomy, and 2026 Kenyan tank cost benchmarks.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: 100 m² Mabati Roof in Kiambu County
workedExample.scenario: A family of 4 in Kiambu (MAM 480 mm, OND 340 mm, Annual 1,040 mm) has a 100 m² mabati roof (0.90 runoff, 5% first-flush loss):
steps: MAM long-rains harvest: 100 m² × 480 mm × 0.90 × 0.95 = 41,040 litres.
Annual harvest: 100 m² × 1,040 mm × 0.90 × 0.95 = 88,920 litres.
A 10,000 L tank (KES 105,000 benchmark) fills over 4× during MAM alone and stores ~50 days of drinking/cooking water at 200 L/day.
workedExample.takeaway: Even a modest 100 m² mabati roof in central or western Kenya can harvest 80,000+ litres per year—making storage capacity, not roof area, the main bottleneck.

complianceTips: Install a simple first-flush diverter and fine mesh leaf screen on downpipes to keep dust and bird droppings out of the tank.
Always place 5,000 L and 10,000 L plastic tanks on a level, reinforced concrete slab wider than the tank base to preserve manufacturer warranty.
notes: Runoff coefficients: Mabati (corrugated iron) 0.90, Clay/Concrete Tiles 0.85, Concrete Flat Roof 0.80.
2026 Kenyan retail tank benchmarks: 1,500 L (KES 19,185), 3,000 L (KES 29,541), 5,000 L (KES 55,417), and 10,000 L (KES 105,000).

faq.question: How do I calculate how much rainwater my mabati roof collects in Kenya?
faq.answer: Multiply your roof's horizontal footprint (m²) × rainfall (mm) × 0.90 (mabati runoff coefficient) × 0.95 (first-flush allowance). For example, 100 m² × 400 mm × 0.90 × 0.95 = 34,200 litres.

faq.question: What size water tank is best for a typical Kenyan rural or peri-urban home?
faq.answer: For a 4-person household, a 5,000 L tank (KES 55,417 benchmark) covers 2–3 weeks of essential use, while a 10,000 L tank (KES 105,000 benchmark) provides 1.5–2 months of dry-spell resilience.

faq.question: Why is rainwater harvesting sizing different between Turkana and Kisii?
faq.answer: Kisii receives ~1,400 mm/year with short 35-day dry spells, so tanks refill frequently. Arid counties like Turkana (~250 mm/year) experience 150+ day dry spells and need larger catchment roofs and bigger storage per person.

fertilizer-seed-breakeven.notesTitle: NFSP e-Voucher Subsidized Fertilizer (KES 2,500) & KALRO Crop Margin Guide
overview: Input prices make or break smallholder farm profitability in Kenya. Under the National Fertilizer Subsidy Programme (NFSP), registered farmers redeem 50 kg bags via e-Voucher at KES 2,500—less than half the commercial agrovet price of DAP (KES 6,250), NPK (KES 6,000), or CAN (KES 5,490).

This calculator pairs official KALRO spacing, seed rates per acre, and yield bands for Maize, Beans, Irish Potatoes, and Bulb Onions against NCPB maize floor prices (KES 4,000/90 kg bag) to show your exact break-even yield and net profit per acre.

Review seed/fertilizer quantities, total cost per acre, break-even bags/kg, and net profit across Low, Average, and High KALRO yields.

workedExample.title: Worked Example: 1 Acre of Maize — e-Voucher vs Commercial Fertilizer
workedExample.scenario: Planting 1 acre of KALRO H614D maize (10 kg seed, 1 bag planting DAP, 1 bag top-dress CAN, KES 14,000 land prep/weeding/harvest):
steps: Commercial fertilizer cost: KES 6,250 (DAP) + KES 5,490 (CAN) = KES 11,740 -> Total cost = KES 28,740 (break-even 7.2 bags at KES 4,000).
NFSP e-Voucher cost: 2 bags × KES 2,500 = KES 5,000 -> Total cost = KES 22,000 (break-even 5.5 bags at KES 4,000).
